## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by pale tan to brownish wings with fine wavy or striated lines, subtle mottling, and a delicate triangular resting posture. In Florida, the Beautiful Undulambia Moth is likely found in warm wooded, shrubby, or semi-open habitats such as hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, gardens, parks, and wetland margins where adults may come to lights. Its caterpillar host plants appear poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small nocturnal plant-feeding moth whose larvae likely feed concealed on foliage or low vegetation, while adults and larvae support birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
